diagrams.title: **A2A between the agents, MCP to the tools, OAuth at every door
diagrams.caption: **A2A between the agents, MCP to the tools, OAuth at every door.** Three separate runtimes, each in its own microVMs, each scaling on its own.
diagrams.svg:

Its tool ask_stock_agent calls the Stock Agent over A2A. The Stock Agent, an A2A agent on port 9001 locally and 9000 on AgentCore, has the http_request tool plus the MCP stock tools. It reaches the Stock Tools MCP server over Streamable HTTP on port 8000, path /mcp, which fetches prices with yfinance. diagrams.title: **Three runtimes, one request
diagrams.caption: **Three runtimes, one request.** AgentCore checks the token at every door before any of your code runs.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 360" class="dimmable" aria-label="One deployed request, step by step. 1 Cognito issues a JWT to you. 2 You call the orchestrator's Runtime URL with the token and a session ID; AgentCore validates the JWT against Cognito's discovery URL and allowed client before your code runs. 3 The orchestrator's model decides to call ask_stock_agent, which sends an A2A message to the stock agent's Runtime URL with the bearer token. 4 The stock agent calls get_stock_price on the MCP server's Runtime URL, again with the token. 5 The MCP server fetches the price from yfinance. 6 The answer flows back up to you." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah-data" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah-data" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker><marker id="ah-proto" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah-proto" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker><marker id="ah-tool" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah-tool" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker></defs>

diagrams.caption: **Pool the connections, separate the workloads, lock the keys away.**

diagrams.title: **Nobody calls the agent directly
diagrams.caption: **Nobody calls the agent directly.** Events flow in, failures are parked for humans, and scheduled jobs run only as long as they need.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 420" aria-label="Event-driven pipeline. A document lands in S3. An EventBridge rule picks up the object-created event and sends it to an SQS queue, which absorbs bursts. The agent pulls work from the queue. Messages that fail three times move to a dead-letter queue; a CloudWatch alarm fires, someone investigates, fixes the issue and replays the messages. When processing finishes, a notification goes to users. diagrams.title: **Most production agents do both
diagrams.caption: **Most production agents do both.** These are the same synchronous, polling, streaming and push styles you met in A2A in Section 5.
